findings.heading: Acceptance criterion 28 is not met: Every factual claim in the guidebook carries a source and a date checked, and no number appears that cannot be traced to one
findings.body:
This kit's own acceptance criterion, written in section 7 of the benchmark before anything was built and scored for the first time on 19 August 2026.

The test it names: Read every claim: each must have a citation with a URL and a date; count the untraceable numbers, which must be zero.

verdict.note: The apparatus now exists and is reachable: 38 distinct real URLs against 2 before, a generated 57-source appendix, and BENCHMARK.md embedded in the book. Per-sentence citation is not met — 68 of 76 external-authority sentences still carry no URL of their own.
verdict.evidence: Re-ran the audit on the rebuilt book. Distinct real URLs went from 2, both licence texts, to 38. A Sources appendix generated from 01_research/_data/external-sources.json lists all 57 sources across Apple, Google, standards and formats, and tooling, each with its URL and the date the source itself carried rather than the date it was read. BENCHMARK.md is now file 69 in the embedded kit, so a reader of the book alone can reach the record it cites — that was the specific defect, that the apparatus existed and was unreachable. The four target tokens now carry a URL and a read date in their own $description, so the figures a stranger consumes can be re-checked. What is NOT met is the literal reading: of 76 sentences naming an external authority and a number, 68 still carry no URL in the same sentence. Grading this a pass would be the kind of rounding-up this system exists to refuse.

findings.heading: The manifest gate asserted that Figma publishes neither manifest value, and the false half of that sentence is what stopped the Figma build from ever completing
findings.body: The gate's header, adopt-scaffold.mjs and the plugin README all said the same thing: `api` and `id` are both issued by the Figma desktop app and neither is published anywhere readable, so the manifest cannot be written without it. Because both values were treated as unobtainable, no manifest was ever committed, `node build.mjs` stopped at the gate every time it was run, and CI could only ever run `--code-only` — so the gate itself was never once exercised against a manifest that ships. A claim nobody re-checked blocked a deliverable for the life of the project.

verdict.note: Half of it was false. `api` is published, in two independent places, and adopting it from those is not a guess. `id` genuinely is not obtainable headlessly — but Figma's own samples show an unpublished plugin does not need a numeric one. Fixed 25 August 2026: the manifest is committed, the gate distinguishes a publishable manifest from a development one instead of calling both adopted, and the full build is a CI gate for the first time.
verdict.evidence: Figma's manifest guide documents the `api` field and shows `1.0.0` (https://developers.figma.com/docs/plugins/manifest, read 19 August 2026). Sweeping every manifest.json on `main` in figma/plugin-samples: 32 of 32 declare exactly `"api": "1.0.0"`, with no other value anywhere in the repository. For `id`, the same sweep shows unpublished samples shipping readable slugs rather than numbers — png-crop, bar-chart-sample, pie-chart-sample, document-statistics-sample. Both sources and their read dates are recorded in 13_plugins/figma/scripts/figma-api-version.txt. `cd 13_plugins/figma && node build.mjs` now ends `manifest.json is adopted for DEVELOPMENT: id aninda-studio-build-the-library, api 1.0.0.` and exits 0.

findings.heading: CI's placeholder-manifest test ended in `rm -f manifest.json`, which was harmless only for as long as no manifest was committed
findings.body: The step writes a placeholder over manifest.json to prove the gate refuses it, then cleaned up by deleting the file. That was safe while the manifest was untracked. The moment a real manifest was committed, the same step would delete it out of the checkout — a test destroying the artefact it exists to protect, in the job that is supposed to prove the artefact is sound.

verdict.note: Caught by the new full-build gate the same day the manifest was first committed, before either reached main. Fixed 25 August 2026: the step copies the committed manifest aside, restores it, and then runs `git diff --exit-code` on it so a restore that silently fails is itself a failure rather than a quietly damaged checkout.
verdict.evidence: The step now reads `cp manifest.json /tmp/manifest.committed.json` … `cp /tmp/manifest.committed.json manifest.json` … `git diff --exit-code -- manifest.json` (relative to the step's working directory, which is 13_plugins/figma; the repo-root form is the bug R4-9 records). Proved locally by running the equivalent block with the manifest left overwritten: it printed `FAILED — manifest.json was not restored` and set the failure flag; with the restore in place it prints `ok` and `git diff --quiet 13_plugins/figma/manifest.json` returns 0.

findings.heading: Two gates in verify-all.sh ran a generator with `|| true`, so a build that refused to run printed ok while the same refusal fails the job in CI
findings.body: Both gates work by rebuilding and then diffing against what is committed. With the build's exit code discarded, a build that died wrote nothing, the committed files were therefore unchanged, the diff found nothing, and the gate reported ok. CI runs the same builds as steps of their own, where a non-zero exit fails the job. This file exists precisely so a local pass means what a green run means; a local gate that cannot fail where CI can teaches you to trust a pass CI will not give you.

verdict.note: Fixed 25 August 2026. Both now test the build's exit status first and report the refusal, then diff. The mark gate three lines above them was believed to be the model, and was not: it reported the refusal and then ran the diff anyway, printing ok on the next line. It was fixed the same day — see R5-21.
verdict.evidence: `grep -n '|| true' scripts/verify-all.sh` returned lines 123 and 153 — the Figma bundle build and the claude-code skill bundle build. Proved the new branch fires by replacing 13_plugins/figma/build.mjs with `process.exit(3);` and running the gate: `figma plugin build is current FAILED — the figma build refused to run`, failure flag 1. build.mjs restored and `git diff --quiet 13_plugins/figma/build.mjs` returns 0. `grep -c '^[^#]*|| true' scripts/verify-all.sh` now returns 0 — a plain `grep -c '|| true'` returns 2, both of them prose in comments explaining this very fix, which is why the quoted command discriminates code from comment.

findings.heading: verify-all.sh overwrote the committed manifest to test the gate and put it back without ever checking that the restore worked
findings.body: The local placeholder test does what the CI one does — write a placeholder over a committed file, prove the build refuses it, copy the original back — but CI then diffs the file and this did not. A restore nobody checks is how a working tree quietly ends up holding a placeholder, and the next commit ships it.

verdict.note: Fixed 25 August 2026: a gate of its own, `the placeholder test put the manifest back`, now diffs the file immediately after the restore, matching CI.
verdict.evidence: Proved it fires by leaving the placeholder in place and running the new block: `the placeholder test put the manifest back  FAILED — manifest.json was not restored`, failure flag 1. After restoring, the same block prints ok and `git diff --quiet 13_plugins/figma/manifest.json` returns 0.

findings.heading: The CI job's own comment said the Figma manifest is not committed, three lines above the steps that check the committed manifest
findings.body: The comment explained why `--code-only` was the only build CI could run: the manifest is not committed at all, because it holds an id issued to one person and CI has no way to obtain one. It was true when written. It stopped being true in the same commit that added two steps directly beneath it which read that very file.

verdict.note: Fixed 25 August 2026. The comment now says why the build runs twice, states that the manifest is committed and since when, and keeps the part that is still true: CI cannot obtain a numeric Figma-issued id, and the gate says so rather than implying otherwise.
verdict.evidence: `grep -n 'the manifest is not committed' .github/workflows/ci.yml` now returns nothing. `sed -n '232,240p' .github/workflows/ci.yml` shows the replacement, and the file still parses as YAML.

findings.heading: The README told the reader to build the Figma plugin with `--code-only`, the one flag whose own build says its output will not load in Figma
findings.body: Under "Rebuild everything", the single Node command given to a reader was `node build.mjs --code-only`. build.mjs's own header says the output of `--code-only` will not load in Figma. So the documented way to build the plugin produced a bundle that could not be used, and nothing on the page said so. It was written when the full build could not complete at all, and was never revisited once it could.

verdict.note: Fixed 25 August 2026 in scripts/readme.py, which generates both READMEs. The reader is now given the full build, with one line saying what the flag is for and who runs it.
verdict.evidence: `grep -n 'code-only' README.md` → no match in the rebuild block; the block now reads `cd 13_plugins/figma && node build.mjs`, followed by a sentence explaining that `--code-only` is what continuous integration runs to compare dist/ against what is committed. Regenerated with `./.venv/bin/python scripts/readme.py`; `--check` passes.

findings.heading: The guidebook told its reader to `cd` into a directory that exists on exactly one Mac in the world
findings.body: Under "Rebuilding this book", the shipped guidebook opened its command block with `cd /Users/gru953/Claude/Cowork/Aninda_Studio` — the author's home directory, in a book published for anyone. The sibling block twenty lines above it, for the component harness, correctly assumes the repository root and says no such thing, so the book contradicted itself on the same page. It also put a machine-specific absolute path into a generated artefact, which this project's own rule forbids.

verdict.note: Fixed 25 August 2026 in the source chapter, which is where it was authored — the generator was copying it faithfully. The block now says "From the repository root, as with every command in this book", matching its neighbour.
verdict.evidence: `grep -c '/Users/' 09_guidebook/Aninda-Studio-Guidebook.html` → `1` before, `0` after; the one hit was line 2409, traced to 09_guidebook/chapters/12-applying-it.md:132 with `git grep -n '/Users/gru953' -- 09_guidebook/chapters`. Book and PDF regenerated; the chapters still pass the English standard, and `09_guidebook/build.py --check` and the PDF-versus-book check both pass.

findings.heading: The English standard's own gate printed a count it had typed: 17 paths, for a list of 18
findings.body: The gate loops over the authored English prose and then prints how many paths it covered. The number was a literal in the printf, and the list beneath it had grown to eighteen entries. It is a small number to be wrong about, and it is wrong in the one place this project claims never to be: a figure typed rather than counted, printed as though it had been measured.

verdict.note: Fixed 25 August 2026. The loop counts what it visits and prints that. Caught while adding a nineteenth path — the Claude Design push record, which is authored English prose and was not being held to the standard that governs authored English prose. Both the CI list and the local list now hold it, in the same order.
verdict.evidence: Counting the loop body by hand gave 18 against a printed 17. The gate now prints `english standard: 19 paths` for 19 entries. `./.venv/bin/python 13_plugins/claude-code/skills/aninda-review/scripts/check.py 13_plugins/claude-design/PUSH-RECORD.md` → `FAILURES (0)`, exit 0. `scripts/check_gates.py` still reports that every CI gate appears in verify-all.sh.

findings.heading: The guard added to stop CI destroying the manifest was itself broken, and turned CI red on the commit that introduced it
findings.body: The placeholder test now saves the committed manifest, overwrites it, proves the gate refuses it, and restores it. The line added to prove the restore worked read `git diff --exit-code 13_plugins/figma/manifest.json` — a repo-root path, in a step whose working directory is 13_plugins/figma, because the step begins `cd 13_plugins/figma`. Git could not find that path from there and said `fatal: ambiguous argument`, so the step failed and reported that the restore had not happened. The restore had happened. The check was wrong about the thing it was checking, which is the worst way for a guard to fail: it accuses the code it is watching.

verdict.note: Found by CI, not by the local mirror of the same gate — the local one runs from the repository root, where the path resolves, so it passed. Fixed the same day: the path is now relative to the step's own working directory and carries `--`, which tells git the argument is a path rather than a revision, so a missing file fails as a missing file instead of as an ambiguous argument.
verdict.evidence: Run 32863139436, job `plugins`, step `A placeholder manifest must stop the build`: `fatal: ambiguous argument '13_plugins/figma/manifest.json': unknown revision or path not in the working tree` followed by `::error::the placeholder test did not restore the manifest`. Every other job in that run passed. Reproduced and fixed locally by running the step verbatim from inside 13_plugins/figma: with `git diff --exit-code -- manifest.json` it prints that the gate refused the placeholder and the restore was proved, exit 0. Negative control in the same directory: leaving the placeholder in place makes the check exit non-zero, with no `ambiguous argument`. Auditing all five `git diff` invocations in ci.yml — `grep -n 'git diff'` returns six lines and the first is prose in a comment against the working directory each runs in, this was the only one inside a `cd`.

findings.heading: The guard that proves CI and the local script hold the same gates read only the first line of each CI step, so three real gates were exempt from it
findings.body: `ci_commands()` captured the step body with `(?P<body>.*)$` under `re.M`, and `.` does not cross a newline — so a multi-line `run: |` block collapsed to its first line. Three gates open with `cd`, `cd ` was in the SETUP list, and `main()` dropped them. They were the npm resolve check and both manifest gates: the two newest, added on 19 and 25 August to close exactly the class of bug this file exists to catch. Deleting any of the three from verify-all.sh still printed "all 32 CI gates appear in scripts/verify-all.sh", exit 0.

verdict.note: Fixed 25 August 2026. The parser takes the whole block — every line indented deeper than the `run:` key — and a step counts as setup only when EVERY line in it is setup, tested line by line. `cd ` is out of SETUP entirely, with a note saying why. Where a gate's command names a file several gates name, the step is keyed by its own name instead, because a substring test on `build.mjs` passes even when the specific gate is gone.
verdict.evidence: Before: 32 gates compared, and deleting the full-build gate, the placeholder gate or the npm gate from a copy of verify-all.sh left the guard printing a clean pass, exit 0, each time. After: 36 gates compared, and each of those three deletions produces `1 of 36 CI gates are not in scripts/verify-all.sh`, exit 1. Enumerating the skips now shows only the six genuine installs. The change also exposed a real gap it had been hiding — see R5-2's sibling, R5-20.

The `git add -N` form was proved on a throwaway repository. specimen.py has not been run end to end and this says so rather than implying otherwise: what was proved is that its two new helpers round-trip against all 70 stored paths and that every stored path resolves to a real file. Re-running it fully is the remaining check, and it needs a browser and renders every specimen page.
verdict.evidence: `git add -N` control, in a scratch repository with one committed and one new file under gen/: `git diff --exit-code gen` → exit 0, the hole; `git add -N -- gen && git diff --exit-code gen` → exit 1, closed. specimen.py: importing it and applying `rel(absolute(x)) == x` to all 70 paths in font_facts.json and measurements.json gives 0 problems, and every one resolves to a file that exists. Downstream, `scripts/check_measurements.py` passes and `09_guidebook/build.py --check` passes.

findings.heading: The package gate's own ignore list was shattered by the space in the repository's path, so it fired on the file it was written to skip
findings.body:
`12_packages/build.py` sweeps the two package trees for files the build did not write, which is the drift a one-directional comparison cannot see. It asks `git check-ignore` which of those files are ignored and skips them, and its own comment names the case: "a __pycache__ written by importing the module locally is the obvious case, and failing on it would make this gate fire on a clean tree for a file that can never ship."

The guard was right and it did not work. `git check-ignore` echoes one path per line, and the result was read with `.stdout.split()`, which splits on any whitespace. This repository lives at `/Volumes/Aninda Studio/Aninda_Studio`, and the space in `Aninda Studio` split every returned path in two: `/Volumes/Aninda` and a mangled remainder. The ignored set therefore matched nothing, and the gate fired on exactly the `__pycache__` it was written to skip.

The shape of it is the part worth keeping. It passed in CI every time, because GitHub checks out to a path with no space in it. It failed only on the machine the work is done on. A gate that is green everywhere except where you are standing teaches you to distrust your own tree.

Smallest fix: `.splitlines()` rather than `.split()`. One word.

verdict.note: Measured before the fix: `git check-ignore --stdin` returned the single line `/Volumes/Aninda Studio/Aninda_Studio/12_packages/python/src/aninda_studio_tokens/__pycache__/__init__.cpython-313.pyc`; `.split()` turned that one path into two entries, `/Volumes/Aninda` and `/Volumes/Aninda Studio/Aninda_Studio/Studio/Aninda_Studio/12_packages/.../__init__.cpython-313.pyc`, and the real path was in neither. `.splitlines()` returns the one correct entry. After the fix, `./.venv/bin/python 12_packages/build.py --check` passes with the .pyc still present on disk: "both packages match the source, 39 files, and hold nothing this build did not write." Before the fix the same command with the same file present exited 1. The tree holds one `check-ignore` call and one `.stdout.split()`, both in this file, so the fix is complete rather than a first instance.

findings.heading: The Bangla rule is enforced on the book and the cards and not on a direction spec, so unverified Bangla entered through the one door nothing watches
findings.body:
This repository's rule is that no Bangla is written for it: only strings checked against the Bangla Academy standard appear, and where none exists the English stands with the gap named. 09_guidebook/build.py enforces it — it hard-fails on any unverified Bangla run — and 08_components/build.py records its gaps in _cards.json.

A colour direction spec carries label_bn for every family and for the direction itself, and nothing checks those. When the palette was replaced on 26 August 2026 the new spec was written with Bangla names that had never been verified — প্রাকৃতিক নীল, প্রাকৃতিক ধূসর and the rest. They reached the palette proof and would have reached the guidebook had a second fault not been masking them.

The instance is removed: natural.json now carries empty Bangla labels and a note saying the colours are not yet named in Bangla. The DOOR is still open. Any future direction can carry unverified Bangla and no gate will notice.

Smallest fix: have 05_colour/engine.py check every label_bn in a spec against 06_type/bangla-strings.json, and refuse a string that is not on the list. That puts the rule where the value enters rather than where it is displayed.

verdict.note:
Fixed 28 August 2026, by inverting the rule rather than by adding a check at the door the finding named. The finding was right that the Bangla rule was enforced where words were SHOWN and not where they ENTERED — and with Bangla removed entirely, the question is no longer 'was this string checked?' but 'why is there Bangla here?'. That has no entry door to leave unguarded.

The English-standard checker now FAILS on Bengali script anywhere outside two retained record documents and the studio's own name. The name is allowed as a STRING rather than by exempting the six files that mention it, because six exemptions for one word would each also license any other Bangla in that file.
verdict.evidence: $ ./.venv/bin/python 13_plugins/claude-code/skills/aninda-review/scripts/check.py 01_research  ->  0 failures (Bangla in a retained record). The same checker on a file with an unrecorded Bengali run fails with 'Bangla in a system that ships English'. BANGLA_PENDING in that file, which listed the paths still carrying Bangla mid-removal, is empty.

findings.heading: The research method read guideline pages and not the feeds where the two stores announce things, so an announcement nine days old was missed
findings.body:
Apple announced new App Store creative asset slots on 5 August 2026 — product page header, search results creative, In-App Events, with a new asset best practices page carrying Figma, Photoshop and Pixelmator templates. The benchmark was checked on 14 August 2026 and did not mention them. Google's Play icon design specification, updated 15 June 2026, was missed the same way.

THE FAULT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN CARELESS, and that is the part worth recording. The check read the HUMAN INTERFACE GUIDELINES and the MATERIAL pages — the documents that describe how a thing should look — and not the developer news feed or the distribution pages, which are where both companies announce that a NEW thing exists. A guideline page says what to do with a slot; it does not say a slot has been added. Reading only the first kind of page cannot find the second kind of change, however carefully it is done.

Smallest fix: carry both feeds as sources, which is done — developer.apple.com/design/whats-new/ and the two distribution pages are in external-sources.json with their read dates. The durable fix is the distinction itself: a source list needs pages that announce as well as pages that describe.

verdict.note: Recorded and fixed on the same day, because the gap register had carried the fix since 26 August 2026 and the finding it asked for was never written. A gap that says 'recorded as a method finding' and points at no finding is exactly the kind of half-closed entry this register exists to prevent.
